evidence.summary: cancel(order) sets status='cancelled' unconditionally; the source comment says a paid order is cancelled without a refund.
The user describes Orderly as orders with states pending, paid, cancelled, refunded.

database: none: orders are dicts passed in by the caller

architecture.backend: A module with a states constant and one free function mutating an order dict.

features.name: Order status lifecycle
features.description: Orders carry a status from a fixed set: pending, paid, cancelled, refunded.
features.observed_behaviour: Only the set of states is defined; no transition table or guard exists in the code.
features.business_logic: Allowed transitions are not enforced anywhere in the source.

features.name: Cancel an order
features.description: Cancels an order by setting its status to cancelled.
features.observed_behaviour: cancel() sets status='cancelled' whatever the current status, including paid; no refund is issued.
features.business_logic: No refund for paid orders, no guard against cancelling a refunded or already cancelled order.

error_handling.behaviour: status becomes cancelled, money is kept (no refund)

unknowns: Where order amounts and customers live: the Orderly code defines no fields besides status.
